items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-08-23
items.q: Yeah, I was working with them. Three chumpers, I was in there, Louie and me.

ctx.x: One thing I wanted to ask you about, too, back on Rene and stuff like that. When he played high, say he was playing a dirt, something in dirt's tempo. And he'd play What a Friend We Have in Jesus. Would he catch that solo at the same range as Buddy? Or would he play it up above the staff? Or what?

Well, I tell you how you do. He would play up, up the lead, you know. Well, maybe when he gets around the end of the song, he reaches up and gets some high notes. He could get them. It was a smile for him to go down. He'd what? It was a smile for him to go get a high note, you know. Way up there. He's playing that for Louie and anybody of them playing high notes when he was playing them.
But if he was taking a solo on a dirge or a hymn, a little slow, he wouldn't go up high then in the main part of it. Just the very end, he'd go up high.
